verdicts.reason: X measures signals of an ongoing relationship with the agency (prior meetings, named officials, pilots), while Y measures structural conformity to the notice's questions and section labels, which a first-time commenter could do perfectly.
Citing CFR parts and sections is a formatting/specificity cue that is entirely separable from mounting a developed argument that the statute does not authorize the rule.

X is a composite of several platform-emission cues (trailing docket line, vendor mail headers, odd list delimiters, template slotting) of which the name-city-ZIP tail is only one, so a comment with vendor headers but an institutional signature scores high on X and 0 on Y.
Emotional intensity and first-hand operational experience are orthogonal: a calm practitioner account scores 0 on X and 10 on Y, and an outraged non-participant scores the reverse.
Both score praise, gratitude, or commendation directed at the agency and its staff; the only divergence is a calibration carve-out for the ritual opening thanks, not a different underlying concept.
Both score the extent to which the submitter credentials itself with quantified size, membership, assets, reach, or market share rather than with evidence about the rule.
X scores praise alone, while Y requires the full praise-then-narrow-ask structure and explicitly scores 0 for uniformly supportive comments, which are exactly the ones X scores 10.
Both score the same adversarial legal-vulnerability framing built from precise statutory commands, claims of no agency discretion, and legal jeopardy or remedies.

X counts any coalition-amplification behavior including endorsing allied submissions and describing sector coverage, whereas Y requires explicit enumeration or quantification of membership breadth, so a bare endorsement of another filer scores high on X and 0 on Y.

X is confined to OCR/scan garbling and defines clean born-digital text as 0, while Y also credits email-routing and portal ingestion debris, so a born-digital emailed comment with routing headers splits the two scores.
Both score the foregrounding of multiple quantified organizational-scale figures (members, employees, assets, customers, market share, operational reach) as self-credentialing.

X scores adversarial posture including bad-faith imputation and name-calling with no legal apparatus required, while Y scores legal-brief structure, so a polite statutory brief and an evidence-free accusatory rant land at opposite corners.
Both score the presence of self-derived numeric compliance-cost figures with their basis stated.
Both score whether the comment offers a concrete alternative regulatory design specific enough for the agency to implement rather than mere objection.
Both score how densely the comment situates itself in the regulatory history of the docket through prior rules, earlier filings, amendments, pilots, waivers, and agency precedent.
Both score the same ingest-artifact bundle: OCR corruption, duplicated or corrupted headers, raw email routing, stray page numbers, and malformed spacing versus cleanly rendered prose.
